title.narrative: NICFI 2026 - 28 Imazon - Data, Law, Market and Citizens

description.narrative:
Geography: Brazil, Legal Amazon that covers nine states Thematic area: Support ambitious policies, reduce forest crime, sustainable commodity production Problem: Illegal clearing and land grabbing, weak law enforcement, lack of transparency/incentives for sustainable production. Proposed solution: The core objective is to curb illegal clearing and land grabbing while fostering climate-smart, deforestation-free agriculture through improved governance, enforcement, transparency, and public engagement. Activities include high-resolution satellite monitoring of deforestation and forest regeneration, legal and financial investigations into environmental crimes, support for land regularization, public land allocation, and supply-chain transparency in the beef and timber sectors.
Partners: Instituto Igarapé, Instituto Governança de Terras (IGT) and OMQQ.
The expected effects for the target group of the Project (Outcomes) are: Outcome 1: Public authorities and financial institutions are more effectively enforcing laws and regulations against illegal deforestation and forest fires, resulting in increased investigations, sanctions, and financial restrictions. Outcome 2: Federal and state governments preserve, improve, and adopt land designation and cadastre policies that curb land grabbing and expand secure IP&LC tenure, supporting forest conservation and sustainable natural resource management. Outcome 3: Meatpackers, retailers, and financial institutions face increased market and reputational pressure to shift trade and investment toward deforestation-free production.
Gender equality is embedded in the project’s design, with targets for balanced participation between women and men across activities and training. “Capacity-building will encourage women’s involvement in our activities, including Black, Indigenous, Quilombola and Trans women.” The project contributes directly to biodiversity conservation by reducing deforestation and forest degradation
